subject: botany_2
question_text: What is the group of bacteria found in both the rumen of cattle and the sludge of sewage treatment?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.49, printed question 144. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: One word answers it. The second mark is what they produce — and it is the same gas in both places.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The group
steps.margin_note: The name and both habitats. Four lines.
lines: They are anaerobic bacteria, found in the RUMEN of
cattle and in the ANAEROBIC SLUDGE of sewage
steps.why: Both places are oxygen-free and full of organic matter, which is exactly the habitat these bacteria need.
common_mistakes: Naming Lactobacillus. Methanogens are the answer.
Saying they need oxygen. They are ANAEROBIC.
steps.memory_tip: No oxygen, plenty of organic matter: methanogens.

steps.label: What they do
steps.margin_note: What they produce, and what it is used for in each place.

lines.text: They make BIOGAS, which is mostly methane

lines: Methanogens break down cellulose and other organic
In cattle they help digest cellulose in the rumen.
In sewage sludge they produce BIOGAS, a mixture of
methane, carbon dioxide and hydrogen, which is
steps.why: The same bacteria doing the same chemistry are a digestive aid in one place and a fuel source in the other, which is why the question pairs the two habitats.
common_mistakes: Saying biogas is pure methane. It is a MIXTURE, mostly methane.
Leaving out the rumen role. In cattle they digest cellulose.
